newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore PCS-1 to reach full output soon.
newsitem.headline: Singapore PCS-1 to reach full output soon.

text.p: The Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore (PCS) has started up its number one ethylene plant over the weekend and is expected to reach full production soon, a company official said on Monday.
"Our Complex 1 plant has started up over the weekend and is now loading up. We expect to achieve full production soon," he said in a statement.

The 450,000-tonne-per-year plant was shut down on a week ago for government officials to carry out investigations following the death of two divers while clearing debris at the unit's seawater intake pit.
PCS is a 50:50 joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell and a Sumitomo Chemical led consortium of Japanese companies.
The company in April started up a new 515,000-tonne-per-year ethylene plant as part of a Singapore $3.4 billion expansion to the first complex.
